list.detail: You ran out of road without a clear slide beforehand, usually a too-early turn-in or a slightly wide line.
list.fix: Turn in a little later and aim for the apex; see the line columns in the steering table.

list.detail: No single input stood out: you were near the grip limit (151° steering, 0% throttle).
list.fix: Be smoother with all inputs here, and check the setup if this keeps happening (see Setup).

list.cause: Lifting off the throttle mid-corner (lift-off oversteer)
list.detail: You came off the throttle from 89% to 0% while turning. That shifts weight forward and the rear loses grip.
list.fix: Avoid sudden lifts mid-corner. If you are too fast, ease off gently or brake earlier next lap.

list.detail: You were still braking at 100% with 20° of steering. Braking moves weight to the front, so the rear has little grip while you turn.
list.fix: Do most of your braking in a straight line, then ease off the brake gradually as you add steering.

list.cause: Too much throttle too early (power oversteer)
list.detail: Throttle went from 99% to 99% in half a second while you still had 10° of steering; the rear wheels spun 11% faster than the car.
list.fix: Squeeze the throttle on over about a second, and only go to full throttle as you straighten the wheel.

corners.name: T1
corners.tip: Carry momentum: brake lightly or just lift, use one smooth steering input, and let the car run to the outside on exit. Over-slowing here costs a lot.

findings.title: T4: slow to build brake pressure (1.98 s)
findings.detail: Get to peak pressure in about 0.1-0.2 s. The car has the most grip when it is fastest, so the first part of the braking zone is where to brake hardest.

findings.title: T8: slow to build brake pressure (0.44 s)

setup.title: No consistent balance problem detected
setup.detail: Handling looks reasonably neutral from the data. Focus on driving technique first.

setup.title: RL: inside only 0.9°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: RR: inside only 1.1°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 4 of 8 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T1, T3, T4, T10. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: Fast, decisive brake application (T2, T6, T7)
pros.detail: You reach peak pressure in under 0.2 s. That is exactly right: the first part of the braking zone is where the tyres have the most grip.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 10 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: Very few locked wheels
pros.detail: You are not flat-spotting tyres under braking.

cons.title: Coasting: 27.3% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 730 m per lap in T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8, T9, T10. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Rear wheelspin on exit in 3 corners
cons.detail: T3, T4, T9. Spinning wheels don't accelerate the car; they just cook the tyres.

cons.title: Throttle on-off-on at the apex (T2, T3)
cons.detail: You pick up the throttle, lift, then reapply. That unsettles the car and usually means you went to the throttle too hard or too early.

cons.title: Slow to build brake pressure (T4, T8, T10)
cons.detail: It takes you 1.98 s / 0.44 s / 1.56 s to reach peak. Aim for 0.1-0.2 s.

cons.title: Running wide of the apex (T5)
cons.detail: T5: 3.1 m wider than your best lap. Missing the apex makes the corner longer and slower.

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T7, T10)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T6, T4, T2, T5, T1
cons.detail: T6: 0.64 s between your average and best pass; T4: 0.57 s between your average and best pass; T2: 0.53 s between your average and best pass; T5: 0.50 s between your average and best pass; T1: 0.34 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T2, T10.

improve.title: Squeeze the throttle on exits
improve.target: Rear tyres within ~10°C of the fronts; no wheelspin flags
improve.how: In slow corners take about a second to go from 0 to 100% throttle, and only go to full once the steering is unwinding. Short-shift (change up early) out of hairpins. Consider turning traction control on while you learn.

improve.title: Hit the apex
improve.target: Within 0.5 m of your best line at every apex
improve.how: In T5, turn in slightly later and aim the car at the inside kerb. If you still can't reach it, you're carrying too much speed in: brake a touch more.

improve.title: Pick fixed reference points
improve.how: For T6, T4, T2: choose one brake marker (a board, a shadow, a kerb start) and one turn-in point, and use them every lap. Move the brake marker 5 m later only when you hit the apex 3 laps in a row.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Going to full throttle while the car is still turning
stopDoing.detail: Add throttle as you take steering lock off, not before.

stopDoing.title: Stabbing the throttle and lifting again
stopDoing.detail: Pick it up once, gently, and only ever add more.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

show.item: Live delta to your best lap
show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Keep these on while you fix coasting (27.3% now): you'll see the gap between the red and green bars. Remove once it's under 8%.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

show.item: Last lap and best lap times
show.why: Glance on the main straight only.
Check after a few laps to see if you are overheating one end.

hide.item: Full standings / timing tower in practice
hide.why: Irrelevant when you are learning. Use the relative (gap to cars around you) only in races.
Useful for your first laps on a new track. After that, learn the track by real reference points instead.
Never read numbers in a corner. Look through the corner to the apex and exit; read the HUD only on straights.
Only matter in long races. Hide them in practice to reduce clutter.

settings: Let AMS2 set steering lock for each car, and watch the FFB meter for clipping.

traits.name: Speed
traits.text: Fast. Small mistakes become big ones.

traits.name: Cornering grip
traits.text: Low grip: the car slides early, so be smooth and patient.

traits.name: Braking power
traits.text: Weak brakes: brake early and carry momentum instead.

traits.name: Downforce
traits.text: No downforce: grip is the same at any speed.

traits.name: How forgiving
traits.text: Some mistakes will catch you out.

tips: Low grip: brake in a straight line, turn smoothly, and avoid sudden inputs.
